title: Regional hospital funding framework and child care investment
subtitle: Right turns on red study, speed camera advocacy, Elect Respect pledge, airport infrastructure funding, new councillor sworn in
overview: Council asked staff to study the regional costs of the new Waterloo hospital and of future expansion at Cambridge Memorial Hospital, and to build a policy framework for any hospital funding. It also asked the Waterloo Region Health Network to present its local share plan, total project costs and a community engagement plan. The amended motion passed {{vote:m16}}, and the final version passed {{vote:m17}}.

Council also approved up to $4.4M in debentures to buy up to two modular child care centres to lease to not-for-profit operators {{vote:m11}}. It directed staff to study banning right turns on red at high-collision intersections {{vote:m7}}, adopted the Elect Respect pledge {{vote:m9}}, and asked the province to strengthen automated speed enforcement rules {{vote:m10}}. A lease of 34 Peel Street in New Hamburg for affordable housing was approved {{vote:m8}}.
Joe Gowing was sworn in as a Regional Councillor at the start of the open session. Staff will report in October on the new garbage cart rollout, including what happens to old bins.

decisions.detail: Staff will work with the Waterloo Region Health Network and Cambridge Memorial Hospital on service impacts and a funding policy framework, and the network is asked to present its local share plan, total costs and engagement plan.

Council authorized up to $4.4M in debentures to buy up to two 88-space modular child care centres, leased affordably to not-for-profit operators on land leased from the Waterloo Region District School Board.

Staff will report on prohibiting right turns on red and adding leading pedestrian intervals at high-collision intersections on regional arterial roads, with a preliminary list of candidate intersections.
Council will lease 34 Peel Street, New Hamburg to Love Your Neighbourhood Communities for $1 per year base rent, with a conditional commitment letter to transfer the property.

decisions.item: Airport servicing, debentures and Elect Respect
decisions.detail: Council agreed to fund Woolwich culvert and sanitary trunk design costs near the airport, allowed debentures up to 30 years for large growth projects, and adopted the Elect Respect pledge.
Council asked the province to improve signage rules, require public reporting, and direct speed camera revenues to local road safety.

decisions.item: Kitchener transit hub updates and road matters
decisions.detail: Council supported a Cambridge boundary adjustment, closed part of George Street North, allowed administrative parking penalties in Woolwich, and asked for a Q4 2025 plan on communicating Kitchener Central Transit Hub construction impacts.
Council accepted a $156,750 tender plus taxes for steel column rehabilitation and shifted $53,200 between transit capital projects, with no net budget change.

debate: On the hospital motion, one councillor opposed adding Cambridge Memorial Hospital because it already exists and is funded by the province. Supporters said the new hospital is part of a wider system including Kitchener campus renewal, and that Cambridge will need future expansion.

Staff said the Region currently has no funding program for any local hospital. Past regional contributions came through a three-hospital plan in the early 2000s, with Cambridge Memorial receiving $7.8 million in 2013.

Councillors raised concerns about the cost to taxpayers, with one noting people are living paycheque to paycheque. Another worried that the process should work with area municipalities' staff. The Chair said the motion complements that work and that the local share is the hospital's responsibility.

A delegate asked for a public camping by-law, pointing to Hamilton's as an example. Another delegate supporting Elect Respect questioned whether relying on law enforcement would build respect, and criticized Council's handling of the 100 Victoria Street North site.
On garbage carts, councillors raised concerns about collecting old bins before the March start and about rubber and metal containers. Staff said they would add these issues to an October report.
